name: Indiana
summary: Court rules are the strongest family: rules.incourts.gov serves every statewide rule set as static per-rule HTML (constructible) plus whole-set PDFs, both script-readable. Opinions since mid-2005 come from a plain-GET JSON API behind public.courts.in.gov/decisions, with PDFs on the same host; transfer dispositions are weekly clerk PDFs on in.gov. The official Code, Constitution, Administrative Code and Register (iga.in.gov, iar.iga.in.gov) are JavaScript-only apps that neither route can read, so statutes and the Constitution fall back to Justia (fetch tool only) and the IAC to Cornell LII. MyCase dockets are robots-disallowed.

citation_patterns.label: Indiana court rules, bare short forms (T.R., Trial Rule, Evid. R., App. R., Crim. R., Prof. Cond. R., Admis. Disc. R.)
Reporter citations with Indiana parenthetical (N.E., Ind., Ind. App.)
Bare North Eastern Reporter citation (no court parenthetical)
Indiana appellate docket numbers (old and post-2021 styles)
Memorandum decisions / Westlaw cites with Indiana parenthetical
Indiana transfer history (trans. denied / trans. granted / trans. not sought)

citation_map.notes: Statute forms require the four-part Indiana number (title-article-chapter-section) after 'Ind. Code', 'I.C. §' or 'IC'; Idaho's 'I.C. § 5-219' (two parts) must not route here. Bare rule short forms (T.R., Trial Rule, Evid. R., App. R., Crim. R., Prof. Cond. R.) are context_required; the abbreviated 'Evid. R.', 'App. R.', 'Crim. R.', 'Prof. Cond. R.' forms (even after 'Ind.') are also matched by Ohio's patterns, so examples use the spelled-out Indiana forms. Old-style dockets like 49A02-1509-CT-1234 are matched by this regex but also overlap D.C./N.C. docket patterns — route them only with Indiana context. law_aliases map rule-set short forms to the rules.incourts.gov {set} key. Indiana has no public-domain citation; App. R. 65(D): memorandum decisions issued on or after Jan. 1, 2023 may be cited for persuasive value. 'trans. denied' is Indiana usage but kept context_required as a bare history phrase. Rule forms also accept 'Ind. R. Evid. 702' and 'Ind. R. Trial P. 12(B)(6)'; 'I.C. 35-42-1-1' without § is accepted (four-part number required).

sources.title: Indiana Rules of Court (rules.incourts.gov, per-rule HTML)
sources.official_status_evidence: No official/unofficial statement on rule pages (WebFetch: 'no disclaimer about official status'). Amendment orders are at https://www.in.gov/courts/public-records/orders/rules/.
sources.coverage: All statewide rule sets: Trial Procedure, Evidence, Appellate, Criminal (restyled numbering 1.1… effective Jan. 1, 2024), Professional Conduct, Admission & Discipline, Small Claims, Post-Conviction, Jury, Tax Court, Administrative, Access to Court Records, Original Actions, ADR, Judicial Conduct, Child Support, Parenting Time, etc. Prior versions linked as dated pages ({MM-DD-YYYY}.htm). Local rules: https://www.in.gov/courts/publications/local-rules/ (not probed).

access.pattern_rules: set keys (law_aliases): trial, evidence, appellate, criminal, prof-conduct, admission-discipline, small-claims, post-conviction, jury, tax, admin, records, original-actions, adr, judicial-conduct, child-support, parenting, commercial, problem-solving, trial-denovo. rule = number with '.' replaced by '-' (T.R. 3.1 -> rule3-1; Prof. Cond. 1.7 -> rule1-7; Crim. 1.1 -> rule1-1). Subdivisions ((B)(6)) are on the rule page. Preamble/scope pages: /prof-conduct/preamble/current.htm.
access.navigation: index.htm lists sets -> /Content/{set}/default.htm lists every rule with links.

automation.notes: The bare host root https://rules.incourts.gov/ is a JS shell (0 chars); /Content/… pages are static HTML. rulesqa.incourts.gov is a QA mirror — never use.

hazards: rule pages include ~1.5K chars of navigation before the heading
Criminal Rules renumbered 2024: old 'Crim. R. 4(C)' is now Rule 4 in the restyled set — check the effective-date line

sources.title: Indiana Appellate Decisions (public.courts.in.gov/decisions + JSON API)
sources.publisher: Indiana Supreme Court / Clerk of the Courts
sources.official_status_evidence: Footer: information on this site 'is not to be considered or used as an official court record'.
sources.coverage: Supreme Court, Court of Appeals and Tax Court opinions, memorandum decisions (isMemorandum flag) and some orders, from mid-2005 (earliest Supreme Court row 6/23/2005; help page says collection dates back to 2005). Up to 250 results per query.

access.pattern_rules: Plain GET returning JSON. courtId: 9510 Supreme Court, 9530 Court of Appeals, 9550 Tax Court (from /Decisions/api/Dropdown/Court). Other params: caseCategoryId, judgeId, countyId (dropdowns at /Decisions/api/Dropdown/{CaseCategory|Judge|County}). Without showMemorandum=true memorandum decisions are omitted (Sept 1-5 2026 COA: 7 vs 30 rows). Each row: style, caseNumber (e.g. 26A-DC-00221), date, decision, isMemorandum, courts[] with trial-court cause numbers, opinionUrl (relative: prefix https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/). There is no docket-number parameter: search by party word + date range, then match caseNumber.
access.navigation: API row -> opinionUrl 'api/Document/Opinion?Id=…' returns the PDF (filename Opinion.pdf).
access.read_via: opinion PDFs on the same host (script ok)

automation.robots_txt: Disallows /MyCase/ca…, /Appellate, /Docket, /*.pdf etc.; /Decisions/ and /Decisions/api/… not covered (script check OK)
automation.notes: The /decisions page itself is a Vue app (no rows server-side). Opinion document URLs have no .pdf suffix, so the /*.pdf disallow does not apply. detailsUrl links into MyCase (/mycase/#/vw/CaseSummary/…), whose data calls are robots-disallowed.

hazards: slip pagination only ('Page 1 of 29'); N.E.3d pages must come from elsewhere
Id tokens in opinionUrl are opaque; take them from the API
250-row cap per query: narrow by date
